corrections.reason: The cited paper did not produce the number and does not contain it: PRA 92, 033603 is the method paper, attached two years after the upload in answer to a request for 'a paper describing the AFQMC method with negative U' (PR #23 thread). The energy is VarBench's own computation, run by co-author Yiqi Yang (Zhang group) with AFQMCLAB and described in the VarBench paper's Suppl. S3 E 1-2. Same history and same fix as the sibling repulsive row Hubbard/square_64_P_32_8 AFQMC -33.642(5), whose reference was changed to the Science paper under the 2026-09-21 ruling (option a, corrections.mjs 'FP4-arxiv-2507-02644#2'); this entry applies that precedent to the eleven rows listed in qmbl-verify DECISIONS.md section 1 as '11 Hubbard (PRA 92, 033603) | the cited paper is a dilute continuum gas study', whose ruling (2026-09-16) was on hold because 'the premise is not established'; the PR #23 exchange (the uploader naming PRA 92 as the method paper) and the VarBench SM's own description of these runs establish it. This is a reference change only, not the rejected baseline/contributed flag. Energy, sigma and bound_type stay: the run is sign-problem-free (N_up = N_dn = 32 in the trial determinant), extrapolated to dt -> 0, so exact (stochastic) with its sigma. Independent check: Particle-hole identity at half filling: -183.064(4) + 4 x 32 = -55.064(4) against Qin et al. Table IV, 8 x 8, U = 4, PBC: '-55.05(1)' (1.3 sigma) and VarBench's separate repulsive run -55.063(4) (Yiqi Yang, 2022-03-16; 0.18 sigma; different HS decomposition, so a separate run). Quoted as 'E_AFQMC/N_site = -2.8603(8)' in arXiv:2507.10705 Table 3 ('Raw data of Fig. 6 in the 8 x 8 lattice at half filling'), citing '[78, 6]' (PRA 92 and VarBench); the stored per-site value is -2.860375(63), so the printed '(8)' is the fifth decimal of -2.86038, not a bar (the same paper calls the uncertainty 'around 10^-4'). The HFPS row -183.012992 on this instance is 0.05 above it.

evaluation.code: Quantax (lrux for the Pfaffian updates); version not stated

compute.reported_as: In most simulations, we utilize a CNN similar to the ResNet in Ref. [42,69] with 16 layers (8 residual blocks), kernel size 3x3, channel number C = 32, and in total around 150K parameters. Among 32 channels, 28 of them are transformed into F~vh with N~ = 14 hidden fermions in the studied spinful system, and the remaining channels are used for the generalized Jastrow factor J(n). The symmetry projection explained in Appendix F is also implemented to improve the accuracy. For simulations in III D, we utilize a GCNN [41] as also described in Appendix F. Unless otherwise specified, the total number of samples in each VMC iteration is fixed at N_s = 16384, and the training takes around 10^4 VMC iterations. || arXiv:2507.10705 Sec. II C: "To solve the SR equation, we utilize minimum-norm SR (MinSR) [42] and subsampled projected-increment natural gradient descent (SPRING) [74] with momentum µ = 0.5." || Acknowledgements: "The NQS simulations are performed by Quantax [90], in which the scalable ANNs are implemented by JAX [91] and Equinox [92], and the LRU is implemented by lrux [93]." || quantax (v0.3.1, 81616bf) quantax/operator/operator.py L241-242: "is_valid = ~(jnp.isnan(H_conn) | jnp.isclose(H_conn, 0))" / "segment, conn_idx = jnp.nonzero(is_valid, size=conn_size, fill_value=-1)"
